title: Florida AI Laws

reading.body:
Florida's only AI-related law is a resolution naming the Tampa Bay area a cybersecurity and artificial intelligence innovation region, not a rule that binds anyone.

The measure, S1816, passed on 2026-03-12. It recognizes CyberBay, acknowledges the state's standing in cybersecurity preparedness and digital defense, and affirms public-private collaboration. It creates no obligation, sets no standard, and applies to no one in particular. A reader looking for compliance duties in Florida will not find them here.

That distinction matters for AI because state law is one of the few levers that can shape where compute gets built and how it gets operated. A designation like this signals intent to attract the industry rather than to regulate it. It is the weakest form of legislative action, and it is the only one Florida has taken on AI.

What the data does not show is whether Florida has considered and rejected stricter bills, or simply not reached them. It covers one enacted law and nothing about pending or failed legislation. One data point cannot establish a trend, and it should not be read as one.

Enacted AI laws in Florida

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • S1816: CyberBay passed 2026-03-12

    The Florida Senate recognizes CyberBay as a cybersecurity and artificial intelligence innovation region within the Tampa Bay area, acknowledges Florida's national leadership in cybersecurity preparedness and digital defense, and affirms the importance of continued public-private collaboration to strengthen cyber readiness and economic resilience.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Florida. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
